title: Stock columns have no non-negative invariant: reserved_quantity/available_quantity can go negative
actual: changelog-001 creates inventory.available_quantity and inventory.reserved_quantity as plain INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with no CHECK constraint. InventoryServiceImpl.commit() performs inventory.setReservedQuantity(reserved - q) and setAvailableQuantity(available - q) with no floor; release() does the same for reservedQuantity. The expiry sweep clamps with Math.max(0, ...) but the service path does not. The JPA @Version column only detects concurrent modification, it does not prevent a negative value.
expected: Stock cannot become incorrectly negative - enforced in the database as the last line of defence, and clamped in the application.
trigger: A commit or release that runs after the expiry sweep already returned the hold (sweep commits first, commit() then subtracts from an already-decremented reserved_quantity), or any arithmetic drift between the reserve/commit/release paths.
root_cause: Invariant expressed only in application arithmetic with an inconsistent clamp; no declarative constraint at the storage layer.
consequences: Negative stock counters corrupt the capacity guard (available - reserved >= qty) so subsequent reservations can oversell; the overselling is silent because no check rejects the write.
remediation: Add CHECK (available_quantity >= 0) and CHECK (reserved_quantity >= 0) via a new Liquibase changeset, and clamp the service-side arithmetic with Math.max(0, ...).
regression_test: Concurrency test: N concurrent commits of the same reservation plus a concurrent expiry sweep must leave reserved_quantity >= 0 and available_quantity >= 0; a direct negative write must be rejected by the DB.

title: Reservation row has no version column: the expiry sweep can overwrite a COMMITTED reservation with EXPIRED (lost update) and double-decrement stock
actual: Reservation has no @Version field and the reservations table has no version column. ReservationCleanupScheduler.releaseAllExpiredReservations() selects expired PENDING rows with an unlocked SELECT (findByStatusAndExpiresAtBefore) and then calls reservationRepository.saveAll(reservations) after mutating them to EXPIRED. InventoryServiceImpl.commit() loads the same row without a lock and writes status=COMMITTED. Whichever transaction commits last wins.
expected: A reservation that has been committed must never be reverted to EXPIRED, and a committed reservation's stock must be released exactly once.
trigger: A commit() that starts just before the reservation TTL elapses, racing with the 60-second expiry sweep.
root_cause: No optimistic-locking or pessimistic-locking discipline on the reservation aggregate, and the sweep performs a blind read-modify-write.
consequences: A paid and confirmed order's reservation is marked EXPIRED; the release path then treats it as already terminalized and never restores or correctly accounts for the stock, producing stock inflation and overselling. The reservation can also be released twice against the inventory counters.
remediation: Add a version column to reservations (Liquibase changeset) with @Version on the entity, and make the sweep claim rows with a locking/conditional UPDATE (status = PENDING AND expires_at < now) so only one writer can transition the row.
regression_test: Concurrency test: commit() and the expiry sweep racing on the same reservation must end with exactly one terminal status and a single stock movement.

title: Expiry sweep releases stock without emitting the inventory.released.v1 event - outbox and domain state diverge
actual: InventoryServiceImpl.release() calls publisher.publishReleased(inventory, r, "PENDING") and releaseCommitted() calls publishReleased(inv, r, "COMMITTED"), both writing an outbox row in the same transaction. ReservationCleanupScheduler.releaseBatch() decrements reservedQuantity and flips the status to EXPIRED but never calls the event publisher, so no outbox row is written.
expected: Every stock movement - including TTL expiry - produces the corresponding lifecycle event in the same transaction.
trigger: Any reservation that reaches its TTL and is swept.
root_cause: The scheduler reimplements the release transition instead of delegating to the shared transactional release path.
consequences: shop.inventory.events.v1 under-reports releases; any downstream projection (or reconciliation job) that trusts the event stream diverges from the inventory table. It also hides the release from the outbox-driven audit trail.
remediation: Route the sweep through the same transactional release path so the outbox row is written atomically with the stock change.
regression_test: Integration test: sweeping an expired reservation must leave exactly one outbox row of type inventory.released.v1 with previousStatus=PENDING.

title: Outbox relay holds a PESSIMISTIC_WRITE row lock and an open DB transaction across a blocking Kafka publish
actual: InventoryOutboxRelay.relay() wraps claimOnePending (PESSIMISTIC_WRITE + SKIP LOCKED), the blocking kafkaPublisher.publish() call (future.get(10s)) and the status save in a single TransactionTemplate transaction. The row lock and the DB transaction therefore stay open for the full broker round-trip, up to 10 seconds per event, with a batch size of 100.
expected: The claim transaction is short; the Kafka publish happens outside the lock; the mark-published step is its own transaction.
trigger: A slow or degraded Kafka broker.
root_cause: Claim, publish and mark-published were fused into one transaction to prevent double-publish, trading lock-hold time for correctness.
consequences: Long-running transactions hold row locks and connections; under broker degradation the relay can pin a HikariCP connection for 10s per event and exhaust the pool (default maximum-pool-size=20), and the outbox_events table accumulates PENDING rows behind head-of-line blocking.
remediation: Split into three phases: (1) short claim transaction that flips the row to SENDING and returns it; (2) publish outside any transaction; (3) short update transaction that sets SENT/FAILED. Recover SENDING rows older than a lease timeout on startup. KafkaMessagePublisher already exposes publishBatch for the async fan-out.
regression_test: Concurrency test: with a broker stub that delays 2s per publish, the relay must not hold more than one row lock at a time and the Hikari pool must not be exhausted; a simulated crash between publish and mark must leave the row recoverable.

title: Reservation retry loop swallows the interrupt flag and keeps retrying after the thread is interrupted
actual: withRetry() catches OptimisticLockingFailureException and calls sleep(). sleep() catches InterruptedException, calls Thread.currentThread().interrupt() and returns; the loop then continues to the next attempt and calls Thread.sleep() again, which throws immediately because the interrupt flag is still set. The loop therefore spins through the remaining attempts without actually waiting and finally raises INVENTORY_VERSION_CONFLICT.
expected: An interrupted request thread aborts the retry loop and propagates the interruption.
trigger: The client disconnects and the container interrupts the request thread while a version conflict is being retried.
root_cause: The interrupt flag is restored but never acted upon; the loop has no cancellation check.
consequences: Busy retry loop on an interrupted thread; the caller sees a spurious version-conflict error instead of a cancellation, and the work continues after the client is gone.
remediation: After restoring the interrupt flag, throw the exception (or return) instead of continuing to retry.
regression_test: Unit test: interrupt the thread inside the retry loop and assert the loop stops after one attempt and does not swallow the InterruptedException.

title: reservations table has no index on order_id and no foreign key to inventory.product_id
actual: The reservations table declares indexes on product_id and on (status, expires_at) but no index on order_id, and no foreign key from reservations.product_id to inventory.product_id. The order_id column is written on every reserve.
expected: A reconciliation query that looks reservations up by order id must not require a sequential scan, and the reservation must not be able to reference a product that does not exist.
trigger: Order-service reconciliation or an operational query filtering reservations by order_id.
root_cause: Indexes were created for the reserve/commit path but not for the by-order lookup path.
consequences: Sequential scans on the reservations table as it grows towards the 30-day retention volume; orphaned reservations are possible if an inventory row is deleted by a path that bypasses the service check.
remediation: Add an index on reservations(order_id) via a new Liquibase changeset. Assess the FK separately - inventory.product_id is unique and the service already blocks deletes with active reservations.
regression_test: Migration test asserting the index exists and is used by an EXPLAIN on a by-order_id query.
